prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 公式文本 · 物理量 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "物理量" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 123px
  col 2: header "符号" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 3: header "公式" · longest unbreakable word 65px · one-line width 91px
  col 4: header "单位" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 31px
  col 5: header "说明" · longest unbreakable word 77px · one-line width 274px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 480px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A compact physics reference table for looking up quantities, their symbols, defining formulas, SI units, and brief explanatory notes.","reading":"Readers scan row by row from quantity to symbol, formula, and unit, then read the explanation; cross-row comparison concentrates on the formula and unit columns.","groups":["Columns 1–2: quantity name and symbol together identify the row.","Columns 3–4: formula and unit together state the technical definition.","Column 5: explanatory prose that supports the row but is read after the formula."],"keep_intact":["Formula tokens and subscripts, especially unbreakable segments such as G·m₁m₂/r² and ½mv²","Symbols and units, including the em dash placeholders","Short headers 符号 and 单位","Quantity names where possible, though long names can wrap"],"may_wrap":["说明 prose, which can wrap naturally over several lines","Long quantity names such as 理想气体状态方程","Formulas at spaces or operators when the full expression cannot fit on one line"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[100,52,90,52,185],"idea":"Balanced compromise: keep symbol and unit columns intact, let long quantity names and formulas wrap modestly, and give the explanation enough width to remain readable."},{"name":"B","widths":[80,52,86,52,209],"idea":"Prose-forward: compress the quantity and formula columns to near their safe minimums so the explanation column gets the most space."},{"name":"C","widths":[144,52,112,52,119],"idea":"Integrity-first: keep quantity names, formulas, symbols, and units all on one line, accepting a narrow, heavily wrapped explanation column."}]}
